question: us-policy-positions:housing-land-use.allow-multifamily-in-single-family-zones
definition: yes (preempts true) = a state law in force on 1/1/2026 requires cities to allow at least duplexes (or more units) by right on lots zoned single-family; accessory dwelling unit laws alone do not count. no (preempts false) = no such state law; cities decide their own zoning.
summarySource: State code pages fetched 9/28/2026: ORS 197A.420, Cal. Gov. Code 65852.21, RCW 36.70A.635, 30-A M.R.S. 4364-A, MCA 76-2-304, 24 V.S.A. 4412, A.R.S. 9-462.13; Montana Free Press (3/3/2025, 3/18/2026) on the SB 323 litigation; 'no' answers rest on each state's own zoning statute or section list (weak) because no complete current tracker fetched (Terner Center 2/2023 database is self-described as not comprehensive).

US-OR.note: Cities of 10,000 or more must allow a duplex on every lot where a detached house is allowed, and cities of 25,000 or more plus Portland-metro cities and counties must allow all middle housing (duplexes through fourplexes, townhouses, cottage clusters); medium cities complied by 6/30/2021, large cities by 6/30/2022.

US-CA.note: Every city and county must approve up to two units on a single-family lot ministerially, without a hearing, in urbanized areas (with a companion lot-split rule allowing up to four units); the fetched text reflects a 2026 amendment (SB 1426) that did not change the 1/1/2026 answer.

US-WA.note: Cities of 25,000 to 75,000 must allow at least two units per residential lot (four near major transit or with an affordable unit), and cities of 75,000 or more must allow four (six near transit or with affordable units); each city must comply at its next periodic comprehensive plan update, so a few smaller or later-cycle cities may not yet have been bound on 1/1/2026.

US-ME.note: Every municipality must allow up to two units on a vacant residential lot (four in designated growth areas with water and sewer) and up to two added units on a lot with an existing home; implementation date 1/1/2024, or 7/1/2024 where voters must approve ordinances; a 2025 amendment raised the per-lot allowances.

US-MT.note: Cities of at least 5,000 residents must allow a duplex as a permitted use on any lot where a single-family home is permitted; a Gallatin County court challenge (filed 12/2023) ended with a 3/3/2025 district court ruling upholding SB 323 in its entirety, affirmed by the Montana Supreme Court on 3/17/2026.

US-VT.note: Every municipality must allow a duplex in any district that allows year-round residential use, on the same lot size as a single-unit home, and in districts served by municipal water and sewer must allow up to four units (source history: 2023, No. 47, § 2, eff. July 1, 2023).

US-AZ.note: Cities of 75,000 or more must allow duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes and townhomes as a permitted use on all single-family lots within one mile of the central business district (and on 20% of new developments over 10 acres) by 1/1/2026; a city that misses the deadline must allow middle housing on all single-family lots.

US-MA.note: Weak: The MBTA Communities law requires one as-of-right multifamily district of reasonable size near transit and § 3 now allows accessory dwelling units by right, but no statute requires duplexes on every single-family lot.

US-CO.note: Weak: HB24-1313 sets transit-area zoning-capacity goals (average 40 units per acre) for transit-oriented communities and HB24-1152 covers accessory dwelling units only; neither requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-RI.note: Weak: The state permitted-uses section (version effective 1/1/2026) makes accessory dwelling units and attached single-family units permitted uses but does not require duplexes on single-family lots.

US-NH.note: Weak: The zoning chapter requires workforce housing opportunities and allows attached and detached accessory dwelling units, and multifamily on commercially zoned land, but has no duplex-by-right mandate for single-family lots.

US-MN.note: Weak: The municipal zoning statute has no duplex mandate; Minneapolis ended single-family-only zoning by its own ordinance.

US-NC.note: Weak: The state's zoning article contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-VA.note: Weak: The state's planning and zoning chapter (section list) contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-ID.note: Weak: The state's Local Land Use Planning Act (section list) contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-NV.note: Weak: The state's planning and zoning chapter contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-OH.note: Weak: The state's municipal planning and zoning chapter contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-IA.note: Weak: The state's city zoning chapter contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-KS.note: Weak: The state's planning and zoning article (section list) contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-ND.note: Weak: The state's municipal zoning chapter contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-WY.note: Weak: The state's cities and towns title contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-WV.note: Weak: The state's zoning article contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-MI.cite: Mich. Comp. Laws 125.3101 et seq. (Zoning Enabling Act, 2006 PA 110)
US-MI.note: Weak: The state's Zoning Enabling Act (section list) contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-SD.note: Weak: The state's municipal zoning chapter (section list) contains no requirement that cities allow duplexes or more on single-family lots; cities set their own zoning.

US-NE.note: Weak: Chapter 19 requires larger cities to adopt affordable housing action plans but contains no duplex-by-right mandate for single-family lots.

US-DC.note: There is no state layer: the District's own Zoning Commission writes its zoning regulations, so no higher law requires duplexes on single-family lots.
